answers.answer: Redis is a server program (a TCP daemon) that manipulates abstract data types held in a key space; clients send commands (e.g. SET/GET) over a network connection and the server runs them against data structures in memory. The data set is kept primarily in the computer's memory (main goal: an in-memory database), optionally copied to disk files and to replicas. Problems it targets, per the README: real-time data-driven applications; caching, session management, querying/sorting/analytics, messaging and interservice communication, vector operations; plus type-specific uses (counters, stacks/queues, leaderboards, rate limiters, event sourcing, semantic similarity search/RAG).
answers.where: index.md Overview and Core ideas (data types table); Advantages the maintainers state; understanding.md Purpose

answers.answer: Snapshots (RDB) dump the data set to disk via a forked child (rdbSaveBackground/rdbSave); the Append Only File (AOF) is an alternative mode that logs write commands. Both can be on at once and each can be off. Durability difference: AOF is flushed from beforeSleep and with appendfsync always the write reaches the file before the reply goes out (and a failed write then ends the process); a detailed durability comparison of the two is not stated (the relevant redis.conf-based text is withheld). At startup, loadDataFromDisk loads the AOF (loadAppendOnlyFiles) when AOF is on, otherwise the RDB (rdbLoad); a preload-file setting overrides both.
answers.where: index.md Core ideas ('Disk is an optional copy'); Workflow 2 Flush; persistence workflow (Restart hop); Trade-offs section

answers.answer: src/bio.c provides worker threads that do background jobs: background close(2), AOF fsync and lazy freeing (lazy freeing in background only above LAZYFREE_THRESHOLD = 64, since small objects are faster to free directly). Its ordering guarantee: not stated.

answers.answer: Modules are shared libraries loaded into redis-server at runtime, letting Redis be extended with new commands/functionality (JSON, time series, probabilistic structures, search come as external pinned modules; vector sets is an in-tree module). External modules are pinned in modules/modules.yaml, fetched with make modules-update and built by make; scripts/sync-redis-conf.sh generates redis-full.conf. At startup a loadmodule config line reaches queueLoadModule, and main calls moduleLoadFromQueue. How a module's own data type is saved and restored: not stated (src/module.c is withheld).

answers.answer: aeMain (src/ae.c) loops calling aeProcessEvents, which waits for ready sockets with aeApiPoll (backed by evport, epoll, kqueue or select) and then runs file events and time events. The connection layer (e.g. connSocketAcceptHandler in socket.c) accepts sockets and hands them to acceptCommonHandler, which calls createClient to install readQueryFromClient as the read handler (networking.c). On a readable socket the read handler reads into querybuf, processInputBuffer parses it and processCommand dispatches it. A time event drives serverCron (server.hz times/sec: active expiry, rehashing, starting saves, replication reconnection). One turn: beforeSleep runs (flushAppendOnlyFile, then handleClientsWithPendingWrites to send replies), the loop sleeps in aeApiPoll, afterSleep runs, then ready file events fire (read handler before write handler, inverted by AE_BARRIER), then due time events run.

answers.answer: The type is what a value is (an abstract data structure such as a list); the encoding is how it is represented in memory for that type, recorded in robj's encoding field as the representation used at the moment (e.g. strings RAW/EMBSTR/INT; sets INTSET/HT; lists QUICKLIST, a linked list of listpacks; streams a radix tree of listpacks). Both exist so memory-saving encodings can sit under each data type. Who decides which encoding is used: not stated.

answers.answer: Clustering code is split between src/cluster.c (key-to-slot mapping and request routing, e.g. getNodeByQuery, clusterRedirectClient) and src/cluster_legacy.c (node failure handling: markNodeAsFailingIfNeeded, clusterHandleSlaveFailover, clusterFailoverReplaceYourMaster); src/cluster.h defines the slot hash. keyHashSlot takes crc16 of the key (only the {...} hash-tag part if present), low 14 bits, giving one of 16384 slots. processCommand calls getNodeByQuery, which returns the node serving the slot; if it is this node the command runs, otherwise clusterRedirectClient replies MOVED (or ASK during migration) with the slot and node address. Keys in different slots get CROSSSLOT; multi-key requests during migration may get TRYAGAIN.

answers.answer: Accept: connSocketAcceptHandler -> acceptCommonHandler (rejects if maxclients reached) -> createClient installs readQueryFromClient; clientAcceptHandler refuses non-loopback clients in protected mode when the default user has no password. Read: aeProcessEvents calls readQueryFromClient, which reads into querybuf and calls processInputBuffer. Parse: '*' means multibulk, otherwise inline. Dispatch: on the main thread processCommandAndResetClient -> processCommand (an I/O thread flags the client and queues it to the main thread). Gate checks in processCommand: authentication, ACL (NOPERM), cluster routing (redirect), memory (performEvictions fails and command is deny-on-memory-limit -> OOM), disk errors (writeCommandsDeniedByDiskError), read-only replica, loading. Execute: call runs c->cmd->proc (setCommand -> setGenericCommand -> setKeyByLink, server.dirty++, shared.ok). Propagate: call queues via alsoPropagate; propagateNow feeds feedAppendOnlyFile (appends to aof_buf) and replicationFeedSlaves (multiple commands wrapped in MULTI/EXEC). Before sleeping, beforeSleep runs flushAppendOnlyFile (with appendfsync always the write reaches the file before reply), then handleClientsWithPendingWrites/writeToClient sends the reply.
answers.where: index.md Workflow 2 and 'Main checks in processCommand' table; deep dive (write propagation)

answers.answer: Partly stated: when the AOF grows past auto-aof-rewrite-percentage and auto-aof-rewrite-min-size, serverCron calls rewriteAppendOnlyFileBackground, which forks a child. A manifest file tracks which files are current: one BASE (snapshot from the last rewrite), one or more ordered INCR files (writes since the last successful rewrite); after a rewrite BASE and INCR become HISTORY files, removed automatically unless garbage collection is disabled. The detailed step-by-step of the rewrite (what the child writes, how new writes are handled meanwhile, how the switch happens) is not stated.
answers.where: index.md persistence workflow (Compact the log); 'Life of the AOF files' figure; deep dive AOF lifecycle

answers.answer: replicationCron sees REPL_STATE_CONNECT and calls connectWithMaster, installing syncWithMaster, which (slaveTryPartialResynchronization) sends PSYNC with a replication ID and offset. On the master, syncCommand calls masterTryPartialResynchronization: it accepts when the ID matches and the offset is still in the backlog, replies +CONTINUE, and sends only the missing data, then streaming continues. Otherwise it replies +FULLRESYNC, runs startBgsaveForReplication, and the replica receives the RDB in readSyncBulkPayload. Afterwards replicationFeedSlaves streams write commands; a replica passes its master's stream unchanged to its own replicas.
answers.where: index.md Workflow 4 and 'How a replica catches up' figure

answers.answer: Two mechanisms: on access, expireIfNeeded deletes an expired key on a master (lazy), and activeExpireCycle scans in the background (run from serverCron). How the background cycle limits its own cost: not stated. Consistency: a replica does not expire keys on its own but waits for the master, which sends synthesized DEL operations through the shared replication/AOF propagation feed.

answers.answer: The project chose a mostly single-threaded core and scales by running many cores presented as one system via higher-order features such as Redis Cluster (the manifesto's rationale text itself is withheld). Extra threads: I/O threads (src/iothread.c) read and parse client input but cannot run commands (they queue the client for the main thread); new clients go to the I/O thread with fewest clients; pub/sub, monitor, blocked and tracking clients stay on the main thread; bio worker threads do background close, AOF fsync and lazy freeing; forked child processes do RDB saves and AOF rewrites. Costs/conditions: io-threads does not make commands run in parallel; TLS.md says multi-threaded I/O is not supported for TLS (possibly stale vs an iothread.c comment); helper threads are started after modules load because of an ld.so TLS/dlopen race; forked children add copy-on-write memory pressure (no figure given).
answers.where: deep dive threads section; index.md Trade-offs (throughput limit, fork memory); understanding.md u-choice-1, u-contra-4

answers.answer: Partly stated: the sync-policy trade-off table is withheld (rests on redis.conf). Stated: the log is flushed by flushAppendOnlyFile in beforeSleep, before replies are written, so with appendfsync always the write reaches the file before the reply goes out (AE_BARRIER exists for such fsync-before-reply cases); with always a failed write calls exit(1) because the reply may already be buffered and the change cannot be rolled back. Why it is batched before sleep rather than per command beyond that, and what durability is lost during a background save with the mitigation (no-fsync-on-rewrite type setting) on: not stated.

answers.answer: When maxmemory is set, processCommand calls performEvictions before running a command; it frees keys unless the policy forbids it. If it cannot free memory and the command is marked deny-on-memory-limit, the client gets an OOM error (shared.oomerr); otherwise the command runs. A 32-bit instance with no limit gets a 3 GB maxmemory with noeviction at startup. Memory/instances not subject to the limit as expected: partly stated - forked children add copy-on-write memory pressure (no figure); other exemptions (e.g. replica/output buffers, replicas) not stated.
